narrative.overview: A room of slate surfaces where nothing shouts until something needs attention. Operate surface for a non-technical client; colour is reserved for meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Slate canvas, one card colour a step above it, hairline borders plus a soft two-layer shadow for lift.
State colours carry meaning only; the accent blue appears on focus rings and primary actions.
Compact full-width rows for apps rather than a grid of large cards.
Dependency and blocked-start reasons sit next to the control they explain.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Green, red and amber mean state and nothing else. A decorative use of them makes a healthy box look broken.

rules.name: The Both-Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour lives as a token with light and dark values kept in step; component CSS reads theme colours from Bootstrap's --bs-* variables or --app-* tokens rather than repeating a hex. Known exceptions today: the service-row icon tile's primary tint, the dialog backdrop, and the startup-log popup's fixed dark palette.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Counts and versions use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so they do not jitter as state changes.

rules.name: The Diffuse-Only Rule
rules.body: Shadows are offset and soft. No zero-blur block shadows, no coloured halos except the focus ring.

dos: Do express new colours through a token with light and dark values, and read the primary via --bs-primary or --bs-primary-rgb.
Do put the reason next to a disabled control.
Do route every visible string through the translate service, with en and pt-PT keys together.
Do give every dialog role="dialog", aria-modal and a name from its heading.
donts: Don't use green, red or amber for anything but state.
Don't add hard offset shadows, gradient text, or glass and blur as decoration.
Don't put layout in inline style attributes; use a class.
